# Contact-constrained affine variations: actual hull repair and labeled stress

This note gives an exact finite first-order interface at a compatible
common-normal simplex family. Its new realizability step is an O(t^2)
ACTUAL hull repair: linearized anchored contacts suffice to realize the
prescribed affine fiber velocities, even if the uncorrected finite-time
simplex images fail containment at second order. The resulting dual is a
finite specialization of normal stress, not a new quantitative depth
inequality. A three-fiber example distinguishes source-only stationarity
from stationarity of the whole family.

## 1. Actual data and the finite contact labels

Let P be a finite lattice-complete base, and let K_z, z in P, be positive
d-dimensional simplexes that are exactly the integer fibers of their
convex hull. All K_z have common outward UNIT facet normals n_i,
i=0,...,d. Write

    K_z={x:n_i.x<=h_i(z) for every i},
    F_i(z)=K_z intersect {n_i.x=h_i(z)}.

Its d+1 vertices are denoted v_z,j, with v_z,j opposite F_j(z).
We use ordinary d-volume on every fiber, and retain the original total
mass M=sum_z |K_z|.

For each q, take all extreme points a of the polytope

    a_z>=0, sum_(z!=q) a_z=1, sum_(z!=q) a_z z=q.              (1)

There are finitely many; an empty polytope supplies no constraints.
Compatibility is equivalent to all inclusions

    sum_z a_z K_z subset K_q.                                (2)

Indeed, support sums are linear in a, so their extrema occur at extreme
representations. A representation with a self coefficient reduces to
one of (1), unless it is the trivial representation of q alone.

Call (q,a,i) active if

    h_i(q)=sum_z a_z h_i(z).                                 (3)

For each active label, choose independently a vertex
x_z=v_z,j_z in F_i(z) for every positive a_z. Put

    xi=sum_z a_z x_z in F_i(q).

Each such tuple gives one contact label ell=(q,a,i,(j_z)). These are
actual simultaneous Minkowski contacts. They are not arbitrary edges
of a graph or independently assigned source/target points.

Choose a vector space E of affine fiber velocities, possibly allowing
only one source fiber to move:

    V_z(x)=A_z x+c_z.                                        (4)

For a simplex this parameterization includes every independent affine
facet-normal velocity. Given affine values psi_i on all facets, at
vertex v_j solve the d independent equations
n_i.V(v_j)=psi_i(v_j), i!=j. Interpolate the resulting d+1 vertex vectors
by one affine map V. On each facet, n_i.V and psi_i then agree at its d
affinely independent vertices, hence everywhere. Thus (4) does not lose
the affine facet tests used in the free-source rigidity theorem.

For each contact label define the linear gap

    L_ell(V)=n_i.V_q(xi)-sum_z a_z n_i.V_z(x_z).               (5)

The finite polyhedral cone of contact-feasible first jets is

    C={V in E:L_ell(V)>=0 for all ell}.                      (6)

For a source-only velocity at p, an active inclusion targeting p gives
the inequalities n_i.V_p(xi)>=0. An active inclusion with p as input
gives -a_p n_i.V_p(x_p)>=0. Several such relations may constrain the
same facet, so they cannot be treated as disjoint leaves.

## 2. Exact first-jet realizability by O(t^2) hull repair

For V in E form the candidate fibers

    Khat_z(t)=(I+t A_z)K_z+t c_z,

which are positive simplexes for sufficiently small |t|. For t>=0 take
the ACTUAL convex hull and its actual fibers:

    C(t)=conv union_z ({z} times Khat_z(t)),
    Ktilde_q(t)=C(t)_q.                                      (7)

**Claim.** If V belongs to (6), then, uniformly over the finitely many q,

    Khat_q(t) subset Ktilde_q(t),
    d_H(Ktilde_q(t),Khat_q(t))=O(t^2).                        (8)

All constants may depend on this fixed V and the initial finite family.
They can also be chosen uniformly when V ranges over a fixed compact
subset of E satisfying (6).

Proof. The facets of the candidate target have normals

    n_i(t)=(I+t A_q)^(-T)n_i

and equations n_i(t).(x-t c_q)<=h_i(q). Each vertex of an extreme
anchored Minkowski sum is among the finite tuples

    xi(t)=sum_z a_z [x_z+t V_z(x_z)],

where now each x_z may be any vertex of K_z. Its target-facet deficit
has expansion

    n_i(t).(xi(t)-t c_q)-h_i(q)
      =n_i.xi-h_i(q)-t L(V)+O(t^2),                          (9)

where L(V) has the same formula as (5). If the constant term is zero,
compatibility forces (3) and every positive input x_z to lie in F_i(z):
the sum of their nonnegative facet deficits is zero. Thus this is exactly
one of the listed labels and its linear term is nonpositive. If the
constant term is negative, its strict finite gap controls the expression
for sufficiently small t. There are finitely many representations,
tuples, and target facets, so one common constant bounds EVERY deficit
by C t^2. The inverse matrices in (9) have uniform bounded second-order
remainders on compact velocity sets and small t.

Every point of every anchored sum therefore lies in the target simplex
with all defining support values increased by C t^2. The same holds for
their convex hull, which is Ktilde_q(t). Positivity and nondegeneracy of
the original simplex give a uniform bound on the inverses of its vertex
intersection systems for small t. Increasing all its support values by
C t^2 therefore changes its vertices, and hence its Hausdorff distance,
by O(t^2). This proves (8). The lower inclusion in (8) follows from the
source fiber itself being included in the actual hull. Lattice
completeness ensures that (7) introduces no unlisted integer base.

The converse is equally explicit. If an actual compatible path differs
from Khat_z(t) by o(t) in Hausdorff distance at every fiber, (2) applied
to its contact tuples and the transformed target inequalities gives
L_ell(V)>=0. Therefore (6) is exactly the cone of affine first jets
realizable by such actual paths. It is not merely a formal necessary
tangent cone.

This realization is in the class of arbitrary convex bodies. The repaired
fibers can have additional facets at finite t; we do not claim that they
remain simplexes or preserve the common normal fan exactly.

The repair is genuinely needed even for three consecutive bases. Let

    K_0=T_0={x>=0,y>=0,x+y<=1},
    K_-1=K_1=J=(1/4)T_0+(0,1/4).

Only the midpoint contact with the facet x=0 is tight. Move only the
source by the affine field V(x,y)=(-y+1/4,1). On the entire contacted
segment x=0, 1/4<=y<=1/2, its outward velocity is y-1/4>=0, so (6) holds.
But the candidate affine image has the facet inequality

    x+t y-t^2-t/4>=0.

The fixed endpoint-fiber point (0,1/4) violates it by exactly t^2 for
every t>0. Thus the uncorrected affine path is incompatible, despite its
feasible first jet. The actual middle fiber is conv(Khat_0(t),J), and its
Hausdorff excess is at least t^2/sqrt(1+t^2) and at most O(t^2). This
explicit example rules out replacing the repair proof by a claim of
automatic exact linear-path feasibility.

## 3. Cap masses and original total mass survive the repair

All candidate fibers stay in a fixed bounded region and retain a common
positive inradius. The expanded-simplex proof of (8), or direct simplex
volume continuity, gives

    0<=|Ktilde_z(t)|-|Khat_z(t)|=O(t^2).                     (10)

For EVERY closed halfspace H, with any base tilt and continuous normal,
the corresponding captured-mass difference is between zero and the sum
of (10). This is uniform over H because it is just a symmetric-difference
bound. Hence the actual and candidate total masses, all fixed or moving
cap masses, and depth at every common point differ by O(t^2) wherever
the latter comparison is used. No ambient-section continuity theorem is
needed for this step. First-order upper cover comparisons transfer to
the actual body (7) with exactly the original mass derivative.

Now fix one REGULAR actual critical cap circuit through a deepest witness.
Its caps have equal original raw mass Q=beta M and actual response weights
theta_j. Regularity and the finite cover/slack hypotheses are those of
`candidate 07dbcd642c33993d`.
Proper, strictly full, and strictly empty traces are all permitted; we
do not assume every cap cuts every fiber properly. Define

    W_z(x)=sum_j theta_j 1_(H_j)(z,x)

on the fiber boundary, with surface-null choices irrelevant. The
normalized first response to (4) is the linear functional

    R(V)=sum_z integral_(boundary K_z)
                   (W_z(x)-beta) n(x).V_z(x) dH_(d-1)(x).   (11)

The subtraction is beta times the ORIGINAL total-mass derivative:

    M'(0)=sum_z |K_z| tr A_z
          =sum_z integral_(boundary K_z) n.V_z.

For unscaled cap normals u_j, the coarea convention is
S_j=sum_z H_(d-1)(K_z intersect boundary H_j)/||u_j|| and
theta_j=(rho_j/S_j)/(sum_h rho_h/S_h), where sum rho_j u_j=0.
Strict full/empty fibers contribute to W and to captured body flux
exactly as their statuses require, even though they contribute zero
proper coarea. They are not discarded from (11).

If this one circuit, together with persistent slack covers, controls all
sources at a local minimum, the actual realization (7)--(10) implies
R(V)>=0 for every V in (6). With several deepest witness groups, only
the appropriate joint maximum/minimum response is constrained. We make
no separate-neutrality inference for one arbitrary group.

## 4. Exact labeled multiplier alternative

For any linear response R on E, the following are equivalent:

    R(V)>=0 for every V with L_ell(V)>=0;

    R=sum_ell gamma_ell L_ell on E, gamma_ell>=0.             (12)

This is finite Farkas duality: the dual cone of finitely many homogeneous
linear inequalities is the nonnegative span of their coefficient rows.
No strict feasibility or constraint qualification is needed. If (12)
fails, a V in (6) has R(V)<0, and the actual hull repair realizes its
strict negative first response. If E restricts the moved fibers, the
identity is required only on that subspace; it must not be upgraded to
an identity in untested fiber variables.

When all affine fiber velocities are included, define the physical force
and first-moment matrices

    f_z=integral_(boundary K_z) (W_z-beta)n,
    B_z=integral_(boundary K_z) (W_z-beta)n x^T.               (13)

Then (12) is precisely the pair of labeled identities

    f_z=sum_(ell:target=z) gamma_ell n_i
           -sum_(ell:input z) gamma_ell a_z n_i,

    B_z=sum_(ell:target=z) gamma_ell n_i xi^T
           -sum_(ell:input z) gamma_ell a_z n_i x_z^T.        (14)

In particular every individual contact preserves its normal label,
its integer barycenter q=sum a_z z, and its continuous barycenter
xi=sum a_z x_z. Summing (14) yields

    sum_z f_z=0, sum_z B_z=0, sum_z f_z z^T=0.                (15)

The full labeled form is more informative than these aggregate equations.
It states exactly how the failure of free-source affine neutrality is
funded by active ACTUAL anchored contacts. It neither bounds the total
multiplier mass nor provides a parity budget or a paying contact cell.

Within the general attained-minimum normal-stress framework, (12)--(14)
are a finite first-jet specialization, not a stronger depth theorem.
The finite separation principle already appears in
`candidate 21a9da879344205f`, Section 4. The earlier
`candidate 860152d497c5cff4`, Sections 3--4, uses a
sufficient pairwise cone and a separate strictification direction to
remove contact multipliers on nonfacet endpoint supports. Here all
baseline normals are shared facet normals, so that elimination does
not remove these labels.
The concrete extra implementation fact here is that every vector in
the displayed linearized cone has the actual O(t^2)-repaired realization.
This removes a possible tangent-cone/shape-path gap. The labeled stress
is not itself a boundary-capacity martingale: its positive multipliers
are forces attached to contact tuples, not a measure with already
identified source density, target capacity, and mass normalization.

## 5. Supporting cuts cannot be silently linearized

At an inside or outside coincidence with a positive-area body facet,
an affine normal velocity psi(x) and cap threshold shift s contribute
respectively the actual terms

    integral_F min(psi(x),-s),
    integral_F max(psi(x)-s,0),                              (16)

in the corresponding unit-normal convention. These are not generally
finite piecewise-linear functions of the affine coefficients: the
crossing subset of a facet moves continuously. The finite binary branch
LP for FACET-CONSTANT velocities therefore does not extend literally
to affine facet tilts.

The geometric cone and hull repair in Sections 1--2 still hold. The dual
(12) also applies to any fixed linear allocated response that is actually
supplied by the established nonsmooth stress interface, using the SAME
inside/outside allocation in its body trace and quantile coefficient.
But existence of such a response, and the order of menu selection and
allocation quantifiers, must be justified by that interface. We do not
infer it by freezing convenient supporting allocations or by swapping
minima and maxima. Thus the regular hypothesis of (11) is substantive.

## 6. Smallest contact calibration: positive source stress, but global descent

Use the actual three consecutive fibers

    K_-1=(19/20)T, K_0=T, K_1=(21/20)T,
    T={x>=-1,y>=-1,x+y<=1}, |T|=9/2.

Their midpoint inclusion is equality. The all-normal theorem in
`candidate f89d52b54ff6950f`
gives a genuine canonical critical circuit at the middle centroid,
proper on all fibers, with

    Q=6, M=5409/400, beta=800/1803<Gamma_2=4/9.               (17)

The canonical integer coefficient is -1/10. The largest endpoint depth
is strictly smaller than Q. All response weights are 1/3. On each middle
facet the response profile has the same zeroth and first moments as the
constant Gamma_2; this is the ordinary canonical centroid calculation.
For an arbitrary SOURCE-ONLY affine field V(x)=A x+c, (11) is therefore

    R_0(V)=(Gamma_2-beta)|T| tr A=(2/601) tr A.               (18)

Its contact cone requires n_i.V(x)>=0 on every whole facet of T. It
is enough to check the two facet vertices. Indeed both endpoint facets
are scaled copies, and their midpoint sum is exactly the whole middle
facet. This cone contains no nonzero neutral affine field: if tr A=0,
the integral of the nonnegative normal velocity is zero, so it vanishes
identically on every facet. At each vertex the two independent active
normals then force V=0. An affine map vanishing at three noncollinear
vertices is identically zero.

Equation (18) has an explicit nonnegative contact funding. For facet i
and each of its two vertices v_j, take the actual tuple
((19/20)v_j,(21/20)v_j), whose midpoint is v_j, and multiplier

    gamma_(i,j)=(Gamma_2-beta) H_1(F_i(T))/2>0.               (19)

Summing its two evaluations integrates any affine normal velocity over
that facet. Thus (19) proves the source-only identity (12) exactly.
The failure of free-source neutrality has been absorbed by genuine
contact forces, without forcing beta=Gamma.

It would be incorrect to declare the whole family stationary. The coupled
motion of endpoint radii

    a(t)=19/20-t, c(t)=1, b(t)=21/20+t

preserves the exact midpoint inclusion. For sufficiently small positive t
the same proper critical branch remains active, Q(t)=6, while

    M(t)=5409/400+(9/10)t+9t^2.

Its full-family normalized cover response is

    R=Q'(0)-beta M'(0)=-240/601<0.                           (20)

Thus no common multiplier identity (12) exists on the space of ALL fiber
affine fields for this example. Source-only identities may be perfectly
valid while a coupled contact motion strictly descends. This is precisely
why one cannot eliminate a leaf, or close an induction, from its isolated
contact stress alone.

The example has an affine centroid graph and beta>Gamma_2/2, so it is in
an already solved class and is not an OC obstruction. At a hypothetical
bad attained minimum, (20) must be excluded by genuinely joint stationarity;
one must additionally retain the complete family of labeled contact
constraints and all source-cover responses. Nothing in (12) alone forces
those contacts to have lower dimension, form disjoint cells, or consume
the correct occupied-parity budget.
